transcript: Most decks have too many pictures, too small, placed wherever there was room. The fix isn't design talent. It's a few simple rules.
Before you add any image, ask one question: what would the viewer lose without it? If the answer is nothing, leave it out.
One strong image at full width beats three small ones. Then crop away anything that doesn't support the point.
Pick one layout per slide. If a headline sits over a photo, find the quiet part, or add a contrast band behind it.
Four tiny product photos became one large shot of the Trail Pack. One image, one claim, one sentence of support. The narration does the rest.
Fewer, bigger images make a better video. On Pro, AI directs it, framing each picture as a scene timed to your voice. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
